narrative.overview:
This descriptive label comes from PRODUCT.md's existing direction, not a newly approved metaphor. Burgundy anchors an Arabic teaching workspace on warm ivory, with sage and muted sand organizing supporting information. Spacious bordered cards, Tajawal and calm botanical lesson imagery provide the current visual character. The أثر reference informs craft and organization without supplying its brand.

This is a source-derived record of the new React workspace and separate React Native/Expo application. It does not restyle or supersede the preserved legacy Convex application. Web and native share an identity but currently have distinct literal color and shape values; the native-prefixed tokens preserve that difference. Native numeric dimensions are React Native logical units, although the portable frontmatter serializes them as px.
keyCharacteristics: Arabic RTL reading order and right-aligned native text.
Burgundy actions, quiet green support surfaces and white bordered cards.
Teacher preparation separated from calm student interaction.
Device-local demo status stated in the interface.

rules.name: The Identity Rule
rules.body: Preserve the incumbent burgundy identity and use the appropriate platform's actual tokens. Status is expressed with a text label as well as a tinted background; color alone does not name a lesson's state.

dos: **Do** preserve Arabic RTL text, functional reading order and the existing burgundy identity.
**Do** use the platform-specific values documented here instead of pretending web and native tokens are identical.
**Do** keep status text, selected-state cues and keyboard-visible focus alongside color.
**Do** verify desktop, phone and native-device layouts after final changes before describing them as approved.
donts: **Don't** copy the inspiration project's branding or replace the existing application framework.
**Don't** treat generated illustrations or fictional profiles as real student evidence.
**Don't** promote decorative eyebrow/kicker treatments into reusable design rules; they remain implementation defects under the documenter craft floor.
**Don't** interpret successful typechecking or bundling as a visual, accessibility or native-device test.
